name: WV-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+20 district partisan lean in deep-red West Virginia
Incumbent Riley Moore with a 10-to-1 fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price Moore at roughly 97% to win
Challenger Ace Parsi has minimal resources and no polling presence
model.rationale: The R+20 lean, Moore's incumbency and dominant fundraising, and markets pricing him near 97% all point the same direction, with no polls or ratings suggesting any reason to move. The forecast stays at an 18-point Republican margin.
model.watch: Any unexpected polling showing Parsi within single digits, or major outside spending against Moore, would be the first sign this is closer than priced.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Riley Moore, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored in a West Virginia district that leaned about 20 points Republican at the presidential level. He has raised roughly $1.3 million and holds about $750,000 on hand, while Democratic challenger Ace Parsi has raised about $134,000 with limited cash remaining. No outside groups are meaningfully engaged on either side.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings exist for the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which price Moore's chances near 97%. With a strong Republican environment and the incumbent's financial edge, the race is rated Safe Republican, with an expected margin of about 18 points. Parsi would need a dramatic shift in the political environment or a surge of outside money to make this competitive.
